title: Napoleon Was Their Third Pick
summary: How the 1799 Brumaire coup hired Napoleon as a third-choice general, and how bankers, bonds and the new Banque de France profited from his rule.
description:
Whose man was Napoleon? And who was their first choice?

Somebody went shopping for a general to front a takeover. On the morning of the coup, France’s government bonds jumped, before anyone knew it would work.

Heather thinks somebody knew. Edwin would like a list of who was buying. History, allegedly.

THE PRINTED ISSUE
SIDE EYE: The Loser's Issue. Our Napoleon feature, "Not a Loser. Not Short. Not Alone.", lays out the job posting, the crew, the bond market and the bank, with what we can prove and what we can't, side by side. Bonus: DRESS THE HIRE, a cut-out Napoleon paper doll with HAT NO. 3 (Hats No. 1 and 2 were unavailable). Scissors not included.

Get it on Amazon: https://a.co/d/02FwgFhM
Or search "side eye magazine"

ONE QUESTION FOR THE COMMENTS
Who actually won: the general, the bankers or the bookkeeper? You're not allowed to answer "France."

THE FILES WE KEPT
Napoleon's letters and the government newspaper: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier and Le Moniteur, via archive.org
The coup and the bankers: Mark Stokle, The Bankers of Brumaire, University of Glasgow
Money and law: Vandal; Marion, Histoire financière
The official fan club: Fondation Napoléon
Louisiana: Founders Online (Livingston to Madison); Henry Adams
The silver: Carlos Marichal
The London bank: The Baring Archive
The Council of State: Pelet de la Lozère
Images: Wikimedia Commons, Rijksmuseum, Paris Musées, Library of Congress and the Musée de Versailles (public domain / CC0)
